# Remembering conversations

A model remembers nothing between calls. A chat feels continuous only because the app sends the conversation again
with every question. So "memory" is something you build: you decide what to keep, where, and how much of it to send
back each time.

## The short way: Agent Chat

The [Agent Chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/agent-chat) extension does everything below for you: it stores the chats, sends
the recent turns with a summary of the older ones, keeps the start of each prompt stable for the cache, and gives each
chat a thread so the built-in model reads only the new question.

```ts
// when a user opens a new chat
const id: string = $agent.newChat({ meta: { user: ctx.auth.id } })

// each question
const chat: AgentChat = $agent.chat(id, { system: preamble, context: (q) => excerptsFor(q) })
if (chat.meta().user !== ctx.auth?.id) throw ctx.httpError(404, "no such chat")
const answer: AgentAnswer = chat.send(question) // or chat.send(question, { onText }) to stream it
```

```go
chats := chatv1.Contract.Must(app)

// when a user opens a new chat
meta, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"user": e.Auth.Id}) // e is the request (*core.RequestEvent)
c, err := chats.New(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.NewInput{Meta: meta})

// each question (check the chat's meta is the caller's first, as above)
res, err := chats.Send(ctx, extkit.Internal, chatv1.SendInput{ID: c.ID, Text: question, System: preamble,
	Context: excerptsFor(question)}) // or chats.SendStream to stream it
answer := res.Answer.Text
```

`$agent.chats.list({ meta: { user } })` lists a user's chats, `chat.history()` reads one back, and
`$agent.chats.forget({ meta: { user } })` deletes them all when the user goes. The rest of this page is how to build
the same yourself, when you want your own collections or rules.

## Keep chats in your app

Store every chat as records, so it survives reloads and belongs to the person who had it. Two collections are enough:

| Collection | Fields | API rules |
|---|---|---|
| `chats` | `user` (relation to users), `title` (text), `summary` (text) | `user = @request.auth.id` |
| `messages` | `chat` (relation to chats), `role` (select: user, assistant), `content` (text) | `chat.user = @request.auth.id` |

Each question then loads what it needs, asks, and saves both turns:

```ts
// pb_pages/_private/chat.ts
const preamble = (ctx: any): string => toString($os.readFile(`${ctx.pagesDir}/_private/preamble.md`))

export function ask(ctx: any, chatId: string, question: string): string {
  const app = ctx.app
  const chat = app.findRecordById("chats", chatId)
  if (chat.getString("user") !== ctx.auth?.id) throw ctx.httpError(404, "no such chat")

  const recent = app
    .findRecordsByFilter("messages", "chat = {:chat}", "-created", 6, 0, { chat: chatId })
    .reverse()
    .map((m: core.Record): AgentMessage => ({ role: m.getString("role") as "user" | "assistant", content: m.getString("content") }))

  const summary = chat.getString("summary")
  const system = preamble(ctx) + (summary ? `\n\nEarlier in this conversation: ${summary}` : "")
  // thread: the built-in model keeps this chat's state, so next time it reads only the new question
  const r: AgentAnswer = $agent.complete({ system, messages: [...recent, { role: "user", content: question }], maxTokens: 350, thread: chatId })

  const save = (role: string, content: string) => {
    const m = new Record(app.findCollectionByNameOrId("messages"))
    m.set("chat", chatId)
    m.set("role", role)
    m.set("content", content)
    app.save(m)
  }
  save("user", question)
  save("assistant", r.text)
  return r.text
}
```

## Send the recent turns, summarize the rest

Sending the whole chat every time works for a while, then gets slow (a built-in model reads every word, every call)
and finally doesn't fit. The usual answer has two parts:

- **A window:** send only the last few turns as messages (six above).
- **A summary of everything before it:** when a chat grows past the window, ask the model to fold the turns that drop
  out into a few sentences, and keep that in the chat's `summary`:

```ts
export function summarize(ctx: any, chat: core.Record, dropping: AgentMessage[]) {
  const r: AgentAnswer = $agent.complete({
    system: "Update the summary of this conversation. Keep names, numbers, decisions and open questions. At most 80 words.",
    prompt: `Summary so far: ${chat.getString("summary") || "(none)"}\n\nNew turns:\n` +
      dropping.map((m) => `${m.role}: ${m.content}`).join("\n"),
    maxTokens: 150,
    temperature: 0.2,
  })
  chat.set("summary", r.text.trim())
  ctx.app.save(chat)
}
```

Run it when a chat passes the window, or every few turns, not on every question: it's an extra call. A
[cron](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-jobs-scheduling/) can do it for idle chats, off the request path.

## Remember across chats

What someone said last week ("I'm on the Team plan", "we deploy with GitHub Actions") can carry into a new chat the
same way you add your docs as context:

- keep short **notes** per user in a collection: a fact per record, written when the user states one, or pulled out
  at the end of a chat with a [schema](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/agent/guides/structured) (`{ type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, maxItems: 5 }`);
- with each new question, find the notes that match it (the same kind of search as in
  [Your own knowledge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/agent/guides/context)) and add them under the preamble: "What you know about this user: ...".

Let people see and delete their notes. Only use a user's notes in that user's chats.

## Keep the start the same

The model keeps the start of recent prompts, and with `thread` a chat's whole state, answers included, and skips
re-reading them when the next prompt starts the same way. So send the preamble first, then the earlier turns exactly
as you sent them last time, then the new question with its excerpts after it: each turn then reads only what's new.

A window that slides by one turn per question changes the start every time. Prefer stretches: send every turn since
the last summary, and when that passes your budget (`$agent.count(messages)`), fold the oldest into the summary and
start a new stretch. Agent Chat works this way (`window`, `summarizeEvery`). See [Prompt caching](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/agent/prompt-caching)
for how it works and how to check it.

A cache isn't memory, though: you still send the turns every time. The window and the summary above decide how much
that is.
